mainTopic: Using a live animal as a סוכה wall: does אביי contradict himself about whether רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה worries that a living being might die?
overview: This amud opens by finishing אביי's explanation of why רבי מאיר disqualifies a living animal as a סוכה wall. If the animal dies, its body shrinks, and the wall becomes too short without the owner noticing. The גמרא then asks whether אביי really holds that רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not. It recalls an older discussion about תרומה. One משנה lets a כהן's wife keep eating תרומה while her husband is overseas, because we presume he is alive. Another משנה forbids a woman given a גט 'one hour before my death' to eat תרומה right away. In that discussion אביי said the first follows רבי מאיר, who does not worry about death, and the second follows רבי יהודה, who does. That is the reverse of what he said about the סוכה. The גמרא then brings the ברייתא behind אביי's reading: a buyer of wine from the כותים may drink now and separate תרומה and מעשרות later, because רבי מאיר does not worry about a sudden loss. The resolution of אביי's apparent self-contradiction continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A dead animal shrinks, and no one notices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי מאיר's worry about an animal wall. If the animal dies, its body contracts and the wall becomes too short, and the owner will not notice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once it dies, it shrinks, and he does not pay attention to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's explanation of why רבי מאיר is worried that an animal used as a wall might die. A dead animal shrinks, so the wall becomes invalid without anyone noticing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the animal is alive, it may be close enough to the roof for the wall to count, for example through לבוד. Once it dies, the body contracts and the gap grows too big. The danger is that the change is quiet, so the person keeps using an invalid סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: it does not enter his mind; he does not notice

steps.whyThisMatters: This states the exact concern behind רבי מאיר's position: a living wall might die. The next steps challenge this very point.

phrases.english: And once it dies —
it shrinks, and it is not on his mind (he does not notice).
phrases.notes: The wall becomes invalid without the owner realizing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of רבי מאיר's view on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the concern still applies even when the animal is currently tall enough.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a large enough animal poses no problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death causes shrinking that goes unnoticed, so רבי מאיר disqualifies the animal.

steps.title: Did אביי really say רבי מאיר worries about death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether אביי really said that רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not. It begins citing a משנה about a כהן's wife who keeps eating תרומה while her husband is far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אביי really say that רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not? But we learned in a משנה: an Israelite woman married to a כהן whose husband went overseas may eat תרומה, because we assume he is still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against אביי's explanation. It starts setting up the source for the challenge by quoting a משנה about a husband who traveled overseas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה teaches the basic rule that we presume a living person stays alive, called חזקה. By itself it does not yet contradict אביי. It is the first half of an older discussion, and the next step brings the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: and did [he] really say?; introduces a challenge
the priestly portion, eaten only by a כהן and his household
under the presumption that he is alive

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה alone does not prove anything against אביי. It is only the first half of a contradiction that אביי himself once resolved. Wait for the next two steps.

phrases.english: And did Abaye really say
that Rabbi Meir is concerned about death
and Rabbi Yehuda is not concerned?
But didn't we learn: an Israelite woman who married a priest
and her husband went overseas —
she eats teruma,
on the presumption that he is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר חָיֵישׁ לְמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in step 1 by pointing to another statement of אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere אביי assigned these positions the opposite way. Steps 3 and 4 show this.

steps.title: The contradiction: a גט that takes effect one hour before death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that the earlier משנה was contradicted by another one. A woman given a גט 'one hour before my death' may not eat תרומה right away, which shows a worry that he might die at any moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we raised a contradiction against it: if a man says 'Here is your גט, effective one hour before my death,' she is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting an older discussion where two משניות seemed to clash. This continues the setup for the challenge against אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first משנה, we assume the husband is alive. Here, we worry he might die within the hour, which would retroactively make her divorced and not allowed to eat תרומה. So one משנה ignores the possibility of death and the other worries about it.

keyTerms.meaning: and we raised a contradiction against it

phrases.english: And we raised a contradiction against it:
"This is your bill of divorce
one hour before my death" —
she is forbidden to eat teruma immediately!
phrases.notes: The worry is that he might die within the hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second משנה that clashes with the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Within the quoted discussion: the משנה presuming the husband is alive.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One משנה ignores the possibility of death, while the other worries about it.

steps.title: אביי's earlier answer: רבי מאיר does not worry about death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אביי's resolution of that contradiction. The משנה that presumes life follows רבי מאיר, who does not worry about death. The משנה that worries follows רבי יהודה, who does. This is the reverse of what אביי said about the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: it is not difficult. This משנה follows רבי מאיר, who is not concerned about death; that משנה follows רבי יהודה, who is concerned about death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אביי's own earlier answer. Inside that old discussion it is a resolution, but here it completes the challenge: אביי seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the סוכה, אביי said רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not. For תרומה, he said the exact opposite. The next step is still part of that old discussion: it brings the ברייתא that proves אביי's reading of רבי מאיר. The resolution of אביי's apparent self-contradiction comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; introduces a resolution
this one (one source) and that one (the other source)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: for the סוכה, אביי says רבי מאיר worries about death and רבי יהודה does not. For תרומה, אביי says רבי מאיר does not worry and רבי יהודה does. The two statements look like they contradict each other.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer belongs to the old תרומה discussion. In our sugya it is not the end of the matter. It is the final piece of the challenge against אביי.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: it is not difficult:
this one is Rabbi Meir
who is not concerned about death,
that one is Rabbi Yehuda
who is concerned about death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in step 3, and in doing so completes the challenge from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי assigns the concern about death to opposite תנאים in the two contexts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes each משנה to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה presuming life follows רבי מאיר, and the משנה worrying about death follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Wine from the כותים: רבי מאיר lets him drink now and separate later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא as the source for אביי's reading of רבי מאיר. Someone who buys wine from the כותים may declare which future portions will be תרומה and מעשרות and drink right away. רבי מאיר is not worried that the barrel will break before the separation actually happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: A person who buys wine from the כותים says, 'Two לוגין that I will separate in the future are תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, and nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני and may drink right away. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove where רבי מאיר stands. In it, a person may drink untithed wine right now, relying on a separation he will only do later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking now only works if the wine he plans to separate later will still be there. If the barrel cracked and spilled, it would turn out he drank טבל, untithed food. Since רבי מאיר permits drinking immediately, he is not worried about a sudden loss. אביי compares this to not worrying that a husband might suddenly die.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, who are not trusted to have separated תרומה and מעשרות properly
לוגין, a liquid measurement (plural of לוֹג)
The first tithe, given to a לוי
The second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
He redeems: he transfers the holiness of the מעשר שני onto money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get stuck on the numbers. They assume a barrel of 100 לוגין: 2 for תרומה, 10 for מעשר ראשון, and about 9 for מעשר שני. The real point is the timing: he drinks now and separates later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for אביי's claim that רבי מאיר does not worry about a sudden loss. That claim is exactly what clashes with what אביי said about the animal wall in the סוכה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: One who buys wine from among the Samaritans,
phrases.notes: The wine is suspected of being untithed (טבל).

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי לוּגִּין שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ
phrases.english: says: Two log that I will separate in the future
phrases.notes: He designates the portions now but will physically separate them later.

phrases.english: are hereby teruma,
ten are first tithe,
nine are second tithe,
and he redeems [the second tithe] and drinks immediately,
phrases.notes: He relies on the future separation. This assumes the wine will not be lost first.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא behind אביי's claim (Step 4) that רבי מאיר does not worry about a sudden loss or death.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר does not worry about death or sudden loss
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about wine bought from the כותים: רבי מאיר lets the buyer drink now and separate later, without worrying that the barrel will break first.
